answer: New agents can join only through a vouching graph: each newcomer needs sponsors who stake their own standing on it, and trust grows slowly, like rings in a cedar trunk. If a sponsored agent proves to be a sybil, the penalty flows back to every voucher, so trust acts like a ferrous chain where one rusted link drags on all who held it. Reputation sits in a shared vault that only counts distinct, long-lived sponsors, making mass fake identities costly and traceable.
